channel.title: Comments on: Resistance is Futile

item.title: By: Lynn cornish
item.dc:creator: Lynn cornish
item.description:
In AA, we are told that willpower is of no help whatever. The only way to recover is through reliance on a power greater than ourselves. We are told we have to "turn our will and our lives over to the care of God." This was a bit difficult for me since I don't have a personal God, but I do know there are forces more powerful than I, for example, I wasn't in charge of the earth spinning. I knew in my first month sober that my problem was feeling disconnected, separate, for addiction is a lonely disease and all these AA people were talking about God. The only way I got through those first six months sober was by living moment to moment, looking up at the liquor cabinet and saying "I am not going to have that now but I might have some tomorrow."
It was really good training in staying present.

item.title: By: carl
item.dc:creator: carl
item.description:
Of course the essence of this study is been 'reported' in scripture for a few thousand years, and undoubtedly through oral tradition far longer. That said, scripture can speak with forked tongue at times. The value of this kind of research is that it helps ground 'eternal truths' in biology and the other sciences.
Still, the ears must want (or rather be ready) to hear. As always, that is the stumbling block. <a href="https://centertao.local/blog/2011/07/09/you-know/" rel="nofollow">We can only truly understand what we already know</a>.
